lessons.titleEnglish: Hail Damage Inspection with an Adjuster
lessons.objectiveEnglishSource: Walk an adjuster across a hail-damaged roof, narrate the storm and findings, and agree on the scope
lessons.speakingEnglishSource: You are the crew lead and the AI is the insurance adjuster: say when the storm came through, show the hits you marked, give counts and measurements clearly, and agree on the scope of work.

words.en: the roof slope (one face of the roof)
The storm came through Tuesday night.
We counted 12 hits in this square.
How many hits do you count?
Can you repeat that more slowly?
Do you agree with the scope?

grammarExamplesEnglish: The storm came through on Tuesday and the hail fell for 15 minutes.
We counted 12 hits in the test square.
readingEnglish: The storm came through Tuesday night, and the hail fell for about 15 minutes.
On Thursday, the insurance company's adjuster arrived at 10 to review the Ortiz family's claim.
Rogelio and Kevin went up with him, with the tape measure and the chalk.
First they checked the gutter and found dents along the whole west side.
On the roof slope that faces west, they marked a test square of 10 by 10 feet.
Rogelio: Kevin, mark each hit with chalk, please.
Kevin drew a chalk circle around each hit.
Rogelio: We counted 12 hits in this square, and here the shingle lost granules.
Adjuster: How many hits do you count on the north side?
Rogelio: On the north side we counted only 3, because the wind was coming from the west.
The adjuster spoke fast and gave several measurements in square feet.
Rogelio: Sorry, can you repeat that more slowly?
Adjuster: Sure, the west side measures 1,200 square feet and the north side measures 800.
Adjuster: According to the insurance company, the west side gets fully replaced and the north side gets repaired.
Rogelio: Do you agree with the scope of work, including the gutter?
Adjuster: Yes, I'm going to note it in the report, and the insurance company will send a copy to the owner.

verbs.exampleEnglish: The storm came through Tuesday night.
The hail fell for about 15 minutes.
We counted 12 hits in this square.
They marked a test square of 10 by 10 feet.
The west side measures 1,200 square feet.

lessons.titleEnglish: Saying No: Unsafe Request from the Homeowner
lessons.objectiveEnglishSource: Refuse an unsafe or improper request from a homeowner politely and firmly, and offer a safe alternative
lessons.focusEnglishSource: Negative commands; subjunctive after no recomiendo que
lessons.speakingEnglishSource: You are the crew lead and the AI is a homeowner in a hurry who asks for something unsafe: refuse politely and firmly with no recomiendo que and no es posible que, explain the risk, and offer a safe alternative.

words.en: I don't recommend that we work in lightning.
It isn't possible for us to skip the underlayment.
I understand your hurry, but I can't do it.
Unfortunately, that's something we can't do.
What we can do is cover the roof with a tarp.
Don't go up until I say so.

grammarExamplesEnglish: Don't go up on the roof in lightning.
I don't recommend that we work on a wet surface.
readingEnglish: It was two in the afternoon, and thunder could be heard far off, to the west.
Mrs. Flores came out of the house in a hurry and spoke with Rogelio.
Mrs. Flores: My children arrive on Saturday, so I want you to keep working even if it rains.
Mrs. Flores: And to save money, put the shingles on without the underlayment.
Rogelio: I understand your hurry, but I can't do it.
Rogelio: In lightning, the roof is the worst place, and I don't recommend that we work in lightning or on a wet surface.
Rogelio: A lightning strike can kill a person, and I'm not going to accept that risk.
Rogelio: About the underlayment, unfortunately, that's something we can't do.
Rogelio: It isn't possible for us to skip the underlayment, because the manufacturer requires it for the warranty.
Rogelio: That shortcut looks like savings today, but later it would be a leak and a much bigger expense.
Rogelio: What we can do is cover the roof with a tarp and come back as soon as the thunderstorm passes.
Rogelio: That way we would finish on Friday, if the forecast helps, and you would have your roof before Saturday.
Mrs. Flores thought for a moment and accepted the alternative.
Rogelio talked to the crew: Don't go up until I say so, and don't leave metal tools on the roof.
Rogelio: The decision is mine, and so is the responsibility.
Rogelio: Kevin, don't take risks for anyone; the safety rule is the same for everyone.

verbs.exampleEnglish: I don't recommend that we work in lightning.
Don't go up until I say so.
Don't leave metal tools on the roof.
Here we never skip the underlayment.
What we can do is cover the roof with a tarp.

lessons.objectiveEnglishSource: Give a crew member private, specific feedback on a crooked course and agree on the fix
lessons.focusEnglishSource: Present subjunctive after wishes and recommendations
lessons.speakingEnglishSource: You are the crew lead and the AI is a crew member whose course is off: talk privately, ask what happened, say what you want them to do with quiero que, es mejor que and te pido que, and get agreement on the fix.

words.en: the exposure (visible part of the shingle)
I want you to look at this course with me.
What happened here, in your view?
It's better that we fix it now.
I'm asking you to measure every three courses.
I'd rather you ask me first.
I'm asking you to check the exposure.

grammarExamplesEnglish: I want you to look at this course with me.
It's better that we fix it now.
readingEnglish: In the afternoon, Rogelio noticed that a crooked course was climbing to the left on Julio's side.
Julio was working fast, but the exposure changed from one shingle to the next.
Rogelio didn't say anything in front of the crew and called him aside.
Rogelio: Julio, I want you to look at this course with me, in private.
Rogelio: It's not to scold you; your pace is good and I trust you.
Rogelio: What happened here, in your view?
Julio: I think I didn't measure from the last line and I did it by eye.
Rogelio: That happens, but with this unevenness the mistake can be seen from the street.
Rogelio: It's better that we fix it now, before the course climbs any higher.
Rogelio: I'm asking you to measure every three courses with the tape measure and to mark the measurement on the shingle.
Rogelio: I'd rather you ask me first, if you're not sure about the alignment.
Julio: All right, I'll take off these four courses and put them back on.
Rogelio: Thanks; correcting is part of the job, and quality belongs to everyone.
Later the company supervisor, Mr. Soto, arrived and saw the shingles on the ground.
Rogelio: Mr. Soto, I'm asking you to check the exposure with me; we're already correcting a course.
For Rogelio, feedback works best like this: clear, in private, and with a solution the worker understands.

verbs.exampleEnglish: I want you to look at this course with me.
It's better that we fix it now.
I'm asking you to measure every three courses.
If you're not sure, ask me first.
I'd rather you ask me first.
